This runs inside the RetrieveTopic Sidekiq job, so a single embed request for a URL not yet in the feed can trigger a full feed crawl and bulk import — potentially minutes of work and dozens of post creations — while the user's embed request is waiting (the controller already rendered 'loading', but the job is blocked and Sidekiq workers are consumed). Worse, every distinct embed_url hit within the throttle window can re-trigger this. The poll should be enqueued as its own job (`Jobs.enqueue(:poll_feed)`) rather than executed inline, and the per-URL retrieval should not depend on a full feed scan.

Script assumes #discourse-comments exists; throws if the host page lacks it

`document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` returns null if the embedding page does not include the expected div, and `comments.appendChild(iframe)` then throws TypeError, leaving a broken embed. The embed snippet should be documented to require the div, and the script should fail gracefully (or create the container) when it is missing.

Spec requires the wrong job file and never tests poll_feed itself

`require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` is unrelated to Jobs::PollFeed (which lives in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) — likely a copy-paste. More importantly, the spec only tests the `execute` guard conditions; `poll_feed` (the actual feed parsing, item URL fallback, content scrubbing, and TopicEmbed.import call) has no coverage at all, including the nil `i.content` crash and the URL fallback logic (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`). Add specs with a stubbed SimpleRSS feed covering: item with link, item with only id, item with no content, and verification that TopicEmbed.import is called with the right arguments.

TopicRetriever spec never tests perform_retrieve, fetch_http, or the Redis throttle

All specs stub out `perform_retrieve` or `retrieved_recently?`; the actual retrieval logic (the exists? check, the PollFeed delegation, fetch_http user lookup and import_remote call) and the `retrieved_recently?` Redis setnx/expire logic are completely untested. The throttle is security-relevant (prevents hammering the remote host), so a regression that removes the expire or inverts the setnx result would go unnoticed. Add specs using mock_redis (already a test dependency) for retrieved_recently?, and stub TopicEmbed.import_remote / Jobs::PollFeed for perform_retrieve/fetch_http.

URL scheme validation regex is over-permissive and inconsistent

`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` — the escaped colons (`\:`) in a regex are just literal colons, so this works, but the pattern is not anchored at the end and accepts strings like `http://` followed by anything, including `http://evil.com" onmouseover=...` (relevant given the XSS in the same method) and `https:///path`. More importantly, the same check is duplicated (with slightly different escaping) in Jobs::PollFeed line 33 (`url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`) and TopicRetriever relies on URI parsing instead. There is no shared URL validator, so the three call sites can disagree about what is a valid embed URL. A single strict validator (scheme http/https, parseable URI, present host) should be used everywhere.

Update-path test does not verify the stored content_sha1 is updated, and update is not isolated from creation

The 'Supports updating the post' test calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, title, "muhahaha new contents!")` and only asserts `post.cooked =~ /new contents/`. It does not verify that `embed.content_sha1` was updated (line 37 of the model uses `update_column`, which skips validations/callbacks — a regression there would go unnoticed), does not verify no second TopicEmbed row was created (the unique index would raise, but the test would surface it only as an error, not an assertion), and because the `let!(:post)` creation runs first, the test depends on ordering. A follow-up import with the SAME content should also be tested to confirm no revision occurs (the `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` guard).

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative URLs and mishandles protocol-relative and default ports

The method rewrites only `href`/`src` values starting with `/`. Protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/x.png`) and scheme-relative paths (`images/foo.png`) are left as-is, so images/links break when the content is viewed on the Discourse origin. Also, the port logic `prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` appends the port for https URLs on port 80 or http URLs on port 443 incorrectly (it checks the numeric port against both schemes' defaults regardless of the actual scheme), and `URI#port` returns the default port when none is specified, so `http://host:80` gets no port (fine) but `https://host:443` also gets none (fine) — the real bug is non-default ports on the 'wrong' scheme and the fact that `uri.port` for a URI without an explicit port returns 80/443, making the condition mostly moot. Use `uri.origin` (Ruby 2.x) or build the prefix from scheme+host+optional non-default port, and handle `//`-prefixed and relative URLs via `URI.join`.

cook_method default of 1 assumes Enum ordering that is not enforced at the DB level

`add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` — the default 1 is meant to be `Post.cook_methods[:regular]` (Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) → regular=1? Discourse's Enum typically starts at 1, so regular=1, raw_html=2). This is correct only if Enum assigns 1 to the first key; the migration hardcodes 1 with no comment or check constraint, so if the Enum definition is reordered, existing rows silently point at the wrong method. Add a comment documenting the mapping, or better, verify in a data migration that the value matches Post.cook_methods[:regular].

cook_method raw_html bypasses sanitization for any post that sets it, with no guard on who can set it

Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and PostCreator (lib/post_creator.rb line 216) copies `@opts[:cook_method]` onto the post whenever present. There is no validation restricting `raw_html` to trusted callers (e.g. staff or the embed importer): any code path that passes user-controlled `raw` together with `cook_method: raw_html` (or any future caller that forwards a request param into opts) stores and renders unsanitized HTML. The `cook_method` option should be stripped from user-facing PostCreator invocations (whitelist it to internal importers only), and ideally raw_html posts should still pass through Sanitize with a strict whitelist before being stored in `cooked`.

discourse_expires_in is called even when rendering 'loading', caching a page that tells the client to reload

`discourse_expires_in 1.minute` runs unconditionally at the end of `best`, including when the 'loading' template is rendered (line 16). The loading page contains a script that reloads after 30 seconds; caching it for 1 minute via the browser/CDN means a user whose import completes 5 seconds later still sees the cached loading page and waits for the reload. The loading response should be marked no-cache (or a very short expiry), while the successful embed view can be cached for 1 minute.

embed_by_username lookup will NoMethodError on nil if the setting is blank

`User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase)` — `execute` guards with `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?`, but `poll_feed` is a public method also invoked directly from TopicRetriever (lib/topic_retriever.rb line 41: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` — that goes through execute, so guarded). However `feed_key` and `poll_feed` are public and the guard lives only in `execute`; any direct call to `poll_feed` (or a future refactor moving the guard) with a blank setting raises NoMethodError on nil.downcase. Move the blank check into poll_feed or use `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.to_s.downcase`.

feed_key is defined but never used — Last-Modified/ETag caching is dead code

`feed_key` builds a Redis key `"feed-modified:<sha1 of url>"` but nothing in the job ever reads or writes it. The apparent intent (per the key name) was to send a conditional GET (If-Modified-Since / If-None-Match) and skip re-parsing unchanged feeds, but `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is unconditional. Every hour the full feed is downloaded and every item is re-imported (TopicEmbed.import does dedupe by content hash, so no duplicate topics, but the work is wasted). Either implement the conditional fetch using feed_key or remove the dead method.

import mutates the caller's contents string in place

`contents << "\n<hr>\n..."` appends to the String passed in by the caller. In Jobs::PollFeed, `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is a fresh string so it is mostly harmless there, but in TopicEmbed.import_remote, `doc.content` (the Readability document's content) is passed directly and gets the footer appended to it; any reuse of that string afterwards sees the mutated value. More subtly, the `content_sha1` is computed AFTER the mutation (line 16), which is correct for change detection, but the in-place mutation of an argument is a hidden side effect that violates the method's contract and will surprise callers (e.g. the disqus.thor importer or tests that reuse `contents`). Use `contents = contents + ...` or `<<` on a dup.

import_remote fetches arbitrary URLs server-side (SSRF) with no scheme or host restrictions

`Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` fetches `url` server-side. `url` originates from the `embed_url` request parameter (EmbedController#best → Jobs::RetrieveTopic → TopicRetriever → import_remote) and from RSS item links in PollFeed. TopicRetriever#invalid_host? restricts the host to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but: (1) that check is bypassable — see the controller finding — and PollFeed passes `i.link`/`i.id` from the feed with only a `^https?://` regex check, so a malicious feed can make the server fetch `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` or internal services; (2) `open` has the pipe-command issue noted above. The fetch must be restricted to http/https and the resolved IP must be validated against private ranges, and the embeddable_host check must actually be enforced on this path.

invalid_host? treats a blank embeddable_host as matching any host

`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` — when `embeddable_host` is blank/nil (the default in config/site_settings.yml is `''`), `nil != "eviltrout.com"` is true, so invalid_host? returns true and retrieval is blocked. That part is fine. But the check is an exact host string comparison with no normalization: `http://EvilTrout.com/...` (case), `http://eviltrout.com:80/...` (explicit default port — URI#host drops the port so this actually matches), or `http://eviltrout.com./...` (trailing dot, which DNS resolves to the same host) will mismatch or match inconsistently. Host comparison must be done on the normalized, downcased host (and the same normalization must be applied in EmbedController's referer check and in TopicEmbed URL canonicalization), otherwise the allowlist is both bypassable (trailing-dot / case tricks against some resolvers) and brittle.

no_throttle is granted based on the requesting user's staff status, but the job runs asynchronously and the check is per-request

`TopicRetriever.new(args[:embed_url], no_throttle: user.try(:staff?))` — the throttle bypass is decided by whichever user happened to trigger the embed request. A staff member viewing the embed page bypasses the 60s throttle, so a staff user (or anyone who can get a staff account to load the page) can force repeated retrievals of the same URL, each performing an outbound HTTP fetch to the embeddable host (a self-DoS / amplification vector against the configured host). The throttle should be keyed on the URL only (as it is), and the staff bypass should either not exist or be rate-limited separately; at minimum the bypass should not be derived from an untrusted request parameter path.

post.user can be nil, causing NoMethodError when rendering an embed

The view calls `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` unconditionally. Posts whose author has been deleted (user_id retained but user row gone, or anonymous/system posts) will raise NoMethodError on nil, breaking the whole embed render (500). Guard with `post.user.present?` or use the existing `post.user` serializer pattern (e.g. `BasicUserSerializer`) / `post.username` (Post#username delegates to user.username and would also fail, so an explicit nil check or `try` is needed).

postMessage resize only fires on window.onload and never on content changes

The iframe height is sent once on `window.onload`. If the embed content grows after load (images loading, fonts, the loading→content transition when the topic finishes importing and the page reloads — that case is covered by reload, but late-loading avatars/images in best.html.erb are not), the iframe keeps its initial height and content is clipped (scrolling is disabled via `iframe.scrolling = "no"` in embed.js). A ResizeObserver or periodic height check should be used, or at minimum re-send after images load.

topic_embeds migration uses force: true, which drops an existing table

`create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` — `force: true` drops the table if it already exists. In a migration this is dangerous: on any environment where the table was already created (e.g. by a previous partial run, a restored backup, or a plugin), running this migration silently destroys all topic_embeds rows (the mapping between external URLs and topics), after which every embed re-imports content as new topics. Migrations should use `create_table :topic_embeds` without force (the same applies to the unrelated change in 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb, which also switched to `force: true`).

true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Login/signup buttons and icons still use float:left inside flex container, causing layout breakage

The `.contents` element is now a flex container (line 17: `@include flexbox()`), but its children `.login-button, button.sign-up-button` (lines 42-47) and `.icons` (lines 53-61) still use `float: left`. In a flex container, `float` is ignored on flex items—floated children become flex items and their float property has no effect. This means the login/signup buttons and the icon list will no longer float left as intended; instead they will be laid out as flex items in DOM order, potentially breaking the header layout. The `float: left` declarations on these elements are now dead code and the visual layout will differ from the pre-flexbox version. These elements need to be converted to proper flex item styling (e.g., using `margin-right: auto` or flex `order` properties) or the flex container approach needs to account for them.

order mixin uses -moz-box-ordinal-group which is incompatible with flexbox order semantics

The `order()` mixin (lines 125-131) emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group: $val` (line 127). The old Firefox flexbox implementation (`-moz-box`) uses `-moz-box-ordinal-group` with 1-based integer values, while the standard `order` property (and `-webkit-order`, `-ms-flex-order`) uses 0-based integers. Passing the same `$val` (e.g., `3` from header.scss line 39, `2` from topic.scss line 30) to both properties means Firefox's old flexbox will interpret the value differently (off-by-one), causing `.panel` and `.extra-info-wrapper` to appear in the wrong visual order in old Firefox versions. The mixin should either not emit `-moz-box-ordinal-group` at all (since `-moz-box` is ancient and rarely targeted), or adjust the value for that property (e.g., `$val + 1`).

The `.panel` rule (lines 35-40) now has `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)`, expecting other flex items (like a `.title` element) to exist as siblings. However, the `.title` selector was deleted from the SCSS, meaning the HTML element with class `title` (the site title/logo area) is no longer styled as a flex item and, more critically, the `margin-left: auto` on `.panel` only works if there are other flex items taking up space. Without the `.title` being a flex item (or any other left-side content), the header layout will collapse or misalign: the logo/title area will not be pushed left, and `.panel` will not be pushed right as intended. The `.title` rule removal appears to be an accidental deletion rather than intentional—the original code had `.title { float: left; }` to position the title, and the flexbox conversion should have kept equivalent styling (e.g., making `.title` a flex item with appropriate flex properties) rather than deleting it entirely.

The percentage-based horizontal padding (`1.5%`) is relative to the width of the containing block, not the element itself, which can produce very different spacing depending on container width. The original `4em` left padding was specifically designed to clear the 45px-wide floated avatar (`.topic-avatar` with `width: 45px` on the `i` element, plus `padding: 5px 0`). With `padding: 0 1.5%`, on narrow containers the left padding may be insufficient to clear the avatar, causing text to overlap or wrap incorrectly under the avatar. The avatar is still floated (line 270: `float: left`), so the text needs adequate left padding to avoid overlapping it.

Removal of .badge-wrapper.bullet margin-top breaks vertical alignment in extra-info-wrapper

The diff removes the `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule from `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper` (lines 33-35 of the new file, removed in the diff). This margin was providing vertical spacing/alignment for bullet-style category badges within the extra-info area. Without it, bullet badges in the topic extra-info wrapper will sit flush against the top of their container, potentially misaligning with the topic title text. The flexbox conversion of the parent (if it were a flex container) might handle alignment via `align-items`, but since the parent is not actually a flex container (see separate finding about `order(2)`), this margin removal causes a visible regression in badge positioning.

flexbox mixin missing -moz-flex standard unprefixed old syntax and -ms-flexbox needs display: -ms-flexbox

The `flexbox()` mixin (lines 100-106) emits `display: -moz-box` (line 102) for old Firefox, but Firefox's old flexbox implementation also supported `display: -moz-flex` as an intermediate unprefixed-ish value before the standard `flex`. More critically, the mixin does not include `display: -ms-flexbox` correctly—it does include it on line 103, but the ordering places `-ms-flexbox` before `-webkit-flex` and `flex`, which is fine. However, the mixin is missing `display: -moz-flex` which was supported in Firefox 18-20 as a transitional value. This is a minor compatibility gap for very old Firefox versions. Additionally, the `-ms-flexbox` value is for IE10, which uses the 2009 flexbox spec with different property names (e.g., `-ms-flex` instead of flex properties), so the `align-items` and `order` mixins' `-ms-flex-align` and `-ms-flex-order` properties may not work correctly with IE10's implementation.

inline-flex mixin emits invalid -moz-inline-box and missing standard fallback ordering

The `inline-flex()` mixin outputs `display: -moz-inline-box` (line 111), which is not a valid value for the `display` property in Firefox's old flexbox implementation (Firefox only supported `-moz-box`, never `-moz-inline-box`), so that declaration is dropped. More importantly, the mixin places the prefixed values before the standard `inline-flex` (line 113), which is correct, but it omits `display: -webkit-inline-flex` ordering issues aside, the real problem is that `-moz-inline-box` is invalid CSS that will be ignored, and older Firefox versions that only support `-moz-box` will fall back to `display: block`-like behavior for `.badge-wrapper.bullet` elements, breaking the intended inline-flex layout in those browsers. The invalid `-moz-inline-box` declaration should be removed or replaced with `-moz-inline-flex` (which Firefox never supported either, so the mixin should just use `-webkit-inline-box`, `-ms-inline-flexbox`, and `inline-flex`).

The `.extra-info-wrapper` element has `@include order(2)` (line 30), but the `order` property only has an effect on flex items (children of a flex container). Looking at the surrounding code, `.extra-info-wrapper` appears to be a sibling of `#topic-title` (which contains `.title-wrapper` with `float: left`), and there is no parent element with `display: flex` that contains `.extra-info-wrapper` as a direct child. The `#topic-title` element itself is not a flex container in this file. Without a flex container parent, `order: 2` is completely ignored, and the intended reordering (presumably to place the extra info/badges after the title) will not happen. This is either a missing flex container on the parent (e.g., `#topic-title` should have `@include flexbox()`) or the `order` property is being applied to the wrong element. The layout intent is broken.

The `.small-action` element is now a flex container (lines 264-265: `@include flexbox()` + `@include align-items(center)`), but its children `.topic-avatar` (line 270: `float: left`), `.small-action-desc .avatar` (line 298: `float: left`), and `button` (line 309: `float: right`) all use `float`. As with the header issue, `float` is ignored on flex items, so these floats have no effect. The `button { float: right; }` (line 309) was intended to push the button to the right side of the small-action bar, but in a flex container this will not work—the button will appear in DOM order (after `.small-action-desc`) rather than being pushed right. The layout of small-action posts (like "X moved this topic" or "X closed this topic") will be broken, with the action button appearing in the wrong position. The flex conversion needs to use `margin-left: auto` on the button or `order` properties instead of relying on floats.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is not a predicate method, so the attribute is always serialized

The method is defined as `def include_website_name` (no trailing `?`), but ActiveModel::Serializers only calls `include_<attr>?` predicate methods to decide whether to include an attribute. Because no `include_website_name?` method exists, the serializer falls back to always including `website_name`. This means `website_name` is serialized even when `website` is blank/nil, and — more importantly — it bypasses the `untrusted_attributes` guard: for a TL0 user viewed anonymously, `website` is correctly omitted (the spec at line 11-15 asserts `website` is not in the JSON), but `website_name` will still be present in the JSON, leaking the user's website host/path to anonymous viewers. The `untrusted_attributes :website` declaration at line 109 is therefore ineffective for the derived `website_name` value. Fix: rename the method to `def include_website_name?` (with the question mark), which will both make the conditional work and make the `untrusted_attributes` mechanism apply correctly (it defines `include_website_name?` returning false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`).

false_positives.candidate:
JSDoc comment for profileBackground was corrupted by the diff — it previously documented websiteName

The diff changed the `@property` line in the doc block above `profileBackground` from `@property websiteName` to `@property profileBackground`. This indicates the original comment block was copy-pasted from a `websiteName` property and was already wrong before this PR (it sat above `profileBackground` but said `websiteName`); the PR 'fixed' the property name but the surrounding description text ('This user's profile background(in CSS).') was already correct. Net effect: the doc block is now consistent, but the change is unrelated to the PR's purpose (moving website-name computation server-side) and suggests the author edited the wrong doc block or the history is muddled. Not a runtime bug; flagging so the maintainer is aware the doc fix is incidental. No action strictly required, but the PR description ('Test 6') gives no context for this drive-by change.

No test covers the sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) or the multi-label public suffix case

The three new tests cover: different domain, exact same domain, and parent-domain (example.com vs forums.example.com). The branch at user_serializer.rb line 144 (same label count, >2 labels — the `www.example.com == forum.example.com` case from the PR title's intent) is never exercised, nor is the `else` branch with a non-matching suffix. Given that branch contains the flawed second-label comparison (see separate finding), it needs tests — including a negative case like `Discourse.stubs(:current_hostname).returns('other.org')` with `website_host = 'www.example.com'` expecting just the host — to pin down the intended behavior before the comparison logic is fixed.

Parent-domain check uses ends_with? on a string, which matches unrelated suffixes

The final branch checks `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`. String `ends_with?` does a naive suffix match, so if `website_host` is `ample.com` and `discourse_host` is `example.com`, `"example.com".ends_with?(".ample.com")` is false — that case is fine — but the real problem is the inverse direction and partial-label matches: if `website_host` is `e.com` and `discourse_host` is `some.com`, `"some.com".ends_with?(".e.com")` is false, but if `website_host` is `com` (a bare TLD, possible from a malformed URL like `http://com/path`... actually URI would parse host `com`), then every `discourse_host` ending in `.com` matches, causing the full path to be shown for an unrelated site. More practically: `website_host = "book.com"`, `discourse_host = "facebook.com"` — `"facebook.com".ends_with?(".book.com")` is false, OK; but `website_host = "ok.com"`, `discourse_host = "facebook.com"` — `"facebook.com".ends_with?(".ok.com")` is false. The actual bug: `website_host = "book.com"` vs `discourse_host = "mybook.com"` → `"mybook.com".ends_with?(".book.com")` is false (good), but `website_host = "book.com"` vs `discourse_host = ".book.com"`... The concrete failure: `discourse_host = "notebook.com"`, `website_host = "book.com"` → `"notebook.com".ends_with?(".book.com")` is false. Hmm — the real issue is `website_host = "com"` or a host that is a suffix of a label: `discourse_host = "example.com"`, `website_host = "ample.com"` → `"example.com".ends_with?(".ample.com")` is false. Actually the genuine bug: `discourse_host = "sub.example.com"`, `website_host = "example.com"` → `"sub.example.com".ends_with?(".example.com")` is true — correct. But `discourse_host = "notexample.com"`, `website_host = "example.com"` → `"notexample.com".ends_with?(".example.com")` is false — correct. The true bug case: `website_host = "e.com"`, `discourse_host = "some.com"` → `"some.com".ends_with?(".e.com")` is false. OK — the actual bug: `website_host = "com"` (host of `http://com/`), `discourse_host = "example.com"` → `"example.com".ends_with?(".com")` is true → full path shown for the unrelated site `com`. Also `website_host = "ple.com"`, `discourse_host = "example.com"` → `"example.com".ends_with?(".ple.com")` is false. So the concrete bug is when `website_host` equals the TLD or a suffix that aligns at a dot boundary of an unrelated domain: e.g. `website_host = "co.uk"` (from `http://co.uk/x`), `discourse_host = "example.co.uk"` → matches, but `co.uk` is a public suffix, not the user's site. The check should compare registrable domains, not raw string suffixes. Consequence: full URL path (which may contain private-looking path segments) is displayed for unrelated websites whose host happens to be a dot-aligned suffix of the instance hostname.

Subdomain-sibling comparison is wrong: it compares only the second label, not the registrable domain

The branch handling hosts with the same number of labels (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) compares `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` with `discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`. For `a.b.example.com` vs `c.d.example.com` (both 4 labels), this compares `b.example.com` vs `d.example.com` and would incorrectly conclude the domains differ even though both are subdomains of `example.com`. Conversely, for `foo.co.uk` vs `bar.co.uk` (both 3 labels, public suffix `co.uk`), it compares `co.uk` == `co.uk` and treats them as the same site, wrongly showing the full path for an unrelated domain. The intent (per the comment 'www.example.com == forum.example.com') is to detect sibling subdomains of a common parent, but the implementation neither strips to the registrable domain nor handles multi-part public suffixes. Consequence: `website_name` shows the full URL path for unrelated domains that happen to share a second-level label (privacy/display bug), and fails to show the path for legitimate sibling subdomains with deeper nesting. A correct implementation needs a public-suffix-aware comparison (e.g. using the `public_suffix` gem if available in Discourse) or a simpler, well-defined rule.

Template now depends on server-computed website_name; any other serializer path that omits it will render a broken/empty website link

The template switched from the client-side `websiteName` computed property (which derived the display name from `model.website` and always worked) to `model.website_name`, which is only present when the `UserSerializer` includes it. `UserSerializer` is used for the full user profile endpoint, but other endpoints that embed user data (e.g. `BasicUserSerializer` for topic posters, admin user lists, search results) do not include `website_name`. If any template or plugin reuses this user template partial with a basic user payload, `{{#if model.website_name}}` will be falsy and the website row will silently disappear even though `model.website` exists. The old client-side fallback handled this gracefully. This is a contract change: consumers of user JSON other than the profile page must now be audited. At minimum, the PR should note that `website_name` is only guaranteed on the full user serializer.

Untrusted-attributes spec does not cover website_name, so the leak described in the serializer bug is untested

The spec at lines 6-16 asserts that `bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background` are absent for a TL0 user seen anonymously, but `website_name` is missing from the `untrusted_attributes` list even though it is declared via `untrusted_attributes` in the serializer (line 109 of user_serializer.rb) and is derived from `website`. Because the `include_website_name` predicate is broken (missing `?`), `website_name` would currently be serialized for anonymous viewers of a TL0 profile — leaking the website host/path — and no test would catch it. Add `:website_name` to the list at line 11 (and the test will then fail until the predicate is fixed, correctly demonstrating the bug).

website URL is parsed with URI three separate times per serialization

`website_name` calls `URI(website.to_s)` three times (lines 138, 143, 146, 149 — four times across branches) plus `website_host.split('.')` repeatedly. Each `URI()` call re-parses the full URL string. For a serializer that runs for every user in list endpoints (e.g. topic views serialize many users via `BasicUserSerializer`, but `UserSerializer` runs on profile pages and admin lists), this is minor but wasteful. Parse once into a local variable and reuse. Not a correctness bug, but a trivial cleanup a maintainer would expect.

The template uses `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` but the controller (`admin-group.js.es6`) no longer has a `members` property (it was removed in the diff: `-  members: null,`). The members are now set on the model (the Group object) via `findMembers()`. Since this is an `ObjectController`, `members` in the template should proxy to `model.members`. However, `findMembers()` is async and sets `members` on the model after the AJAX call completes. If the template renders before `findMembers()` resolves, `members` will be undefined. The `setupController` in `admin_group_route.js` calls `model.findMembers()` but doesn't wait for it. The template should handle the loading state, e.g., `{{#if members}}...{{else}}Loading...{{/if}}`.

true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Pagination next action can set offset beyond valid range

In the `next` action, `offset = Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))`. If `user_count` is 100 and `limit` is 50, and current offset is 50, the next offset becomes `Math.min(100, 100) = 100`. But offset 100 with limit 50 on a 100-user group means the query starts at the 101st user, returning an empty page. The maximum valid offset is `user_count - limit` (i.e., 50 in this case). The `next` action should stop at `user_count - limit` or the `showingLast` computed property should account for this. The `totalPages` computed uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` which is also wrong: for 100 users and limit 50, it returns `Math.floor(100/50) + 1 = 3` pages, but there are only 2 pages (offsets 0 and 50). This causes the UI to show "2/3" and allow clicking next to an empty third page.

true_positives.golden_comment: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Test for remove_member on automatic group uses wrong HTTP method (PUT instead of DELETE)

The test `"cannot remove members from automatic groups"` on line 114-117 uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the route for `remove_member` is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` in `config/routes.rb` (line 49). The test should use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...` to match the actual route. Using PUT will likely result in a routing error (404 or 405) rather than the expected 422, meaning this test is not actually testing the automatic group guard—it's testing that the route doesn't accept PUT. The test passes for the wrong reason.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
totalPages calculation is off-by-one for exact multiples of limit

The `totalPages` computed property uses `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. For a group with exactly 100 users and limit 50, this returns `Math.floor(100/50) + 1 = 3`, but there are only 2 pages (offsets 0 and 50). The correct formula is `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. This causes the pagination UI to show an extra page, and clicking "next" on the last real page navigates to an empty page. The `currentPage` computed has a similar issue with its base calculation.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when name is empty

The `findMembers` method has `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }` which returns `undefined` instead of a resolved promise. Previously this returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. Callers like `setupController` in `admin_group_route.js` (line 13: `model.findMembers()`) and `group-members.js.es6` (line 11: `model.findMembers()`) do not chain on the result, but any future caller that does `.then()` on the result will get a TypeError. More critically, the `removeMember` and `addMembers` methods call `self.findMembers()` in their `.then()` callbacks without returning the promise, which is fine for fire-and-forget, but the inconsistent return type (undefined vs Promise) is a contract violation that can cause subtle bugs.

true_positives.golden_comment: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
add_members and remove_member use params.require(:group_id) but routes define member routes without :group_id segment

The routes in `config/routes.rb` define `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` as member routes on `resources :groups`, which generates URLs like `/admin/groups/:id/members`. However, the controller actions use `params.require(:group_id)`, expecting the parameter to be named `group_id`. With Rails member routes, the id parameter is named `id`, not `group_id`. This means `params.require(:group_id)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` at runtime, breaking both endpoints. The controller should use `params.require(:id)` to match the route definition, or the routes should be defined with an explicit `:group_id` segment.

false_positives.candidate:
Error handler assumes e.responseText is valid JSON without checking

In the `save` action's error callback: `var message = $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors;`. If the server returns a non-JSON response (e.g., a 500 HTML error page, or a network error where `responseText` is undefined), `$.parseJSON` will throw a SyntaxError, masking the original error and leaving `disableSave` potentially stuck (though `finally` handles that). The code should check that `e.responseText` exists and handle parse failures gracefully, falling back to a generic error message.

SQL injection via ILIKE search parameter

The `index` action interpolates the raw `params[:search]` value directly into a SQL string: `groups.where("name ILIKE ?", "%#{search}%")`. While the `?` placeholder protects against classic injection of the search term itself, the `%` and `_` wildcard characters in the user-supplied search string are not escaped, allowing wildcard injection (e.g. searching `%` matches all groups, `_` matches any single character). More importantly, this pattern is fragile and the change from `ilike` to `ILIKE` suggests a hand-rolled query. The search term should be sanitized (e.g. `search.gsub(/[%_]/, '\\\0')`) or use a proper query builder to prevent wildcard abuse and any future refactoring from introducing true injection.

Stray closing div tag inside table row Line 19 contains `` inside the `{{#each}}` loop within a `` structure. A `` inside a `` (without a matching opening `
`) is invalid HTML. Browsers will typically ignore it or hoist it out of the table, potentially breaking the table layout. This should be removed.

Template iterates over 'members' but controller sets 'model'

The template was changed from `{{#each m in model}}` to `{{#each m in members}}`, and the route `group-members.js.es6` now sets `controller.set("model", model)` where `model` is the Group object. The Group model's `findMembers()` sets a `members` property on the group object (line 35 of group.js: `members: result.members.map(...)`). Since the controller is likely an ObjectController or the template context is the group model, `members` should resolve to `model.members`. However, if the controller is not proxying to the model, `members` will be undefined. The template should either use `{{#each m in model.members}}` to be explicit, or the controller should explicitly set `controller.set('members', model.get('members'))` after `findMembers()` resolves. The current code relies on implicit property proxying which may not work depending on the controller type.

Test for add_members on automatic group uses group_id: 1 which may not be automatic

The test `"cannot add members to automatic groups"` uses `group_id: 1`, assuming group with id 1 is automatic. However, group IDs are not guaranteed—the test database may have groups with different IDs, or group 1 may not exist or may not be automatic. The test should explicitly create an automatic group: `group = Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` and use `group_id: group.id`. Relying on a hardcoded ID of 1 is fragile and may cause the test to pass or fail for the wrong reasons depending on test ordering and database state.

Test for remove_member on automatic group uses hardcoded group_id: 1

Same issue as the add_members test: the test `"cannot remove members from automatic groups"` uses `group_id: 1` assuming it's an automatic group. This is fragile—the test should create an explicit automatic group with `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` and use its ID. Additionally, as noted in the other finding, this test uses `xhr :put` instead of `xhr :delete`, so it's not actually testing the remove_member endpoint.

addMembers action has TODO comment indicating incomplete functionality

The `addMembers` action contains `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not clear the `usernames` property after successfully adding members. This means after clicking "Add", the user-selector input still contains the previously entered usernames. If the admin clicks "Add" again without changing the input, the same members will be re-added (though the server should handle duplicates gracefully). The `usernames` property should be cleared after a successful add: `self.set('usernames', null)` or `self.set('usernames', '')` in the success callback of `addMembers`.

add_members silently ignores usernames with surrounding whitespace

In `add_members`, `usernames.split(",")` does not strip whitespace from each username. If the client sends `"user1, user2"` (with a space after the comma, which is common when users type comma-separated lists), `User.find_by_username(" user2")` will return nil and the user will be silently skipped. The member is not added but the response is still `success_json`, so the admin UI shows no error. Each username should be stripped: `usernames.split(",").map(&:strip).each do |username|`.

create action does not set alias_level, defaulting to 0 (nobody)

The `create` action sets `name` and `visible` but does not set `alias_level`. The Group model likely has a default `alias_level` of 0 (which maps to "nobody" in the UI). This means newly created groups are invisible to everyone by default, which may not be the intended behavior. The admin UI sends `alias_level` in the `save` action (via `asJSON()`), but the `create` action ignores it. The `create` action should also accept and set `alias_level`: `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?`.

members action performs two count queries instead of one

The `members` action calls `group.users.count` (line 25) and then `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` (line 26). The `count` query and the subsequent `members` query are separate database queries. While this is acceptable for pagination metadata, the `count` could be optimized by using `group.users.count` only when needed, or by using a single query with `COUNT(*) OVER()` window function (PostgreSQL) to get both total and page in one query. For groups with many members, this is two full queries instead of one. This is a minor performance concern but worth noting for large groups.

offset parameter is not validated, allowing negative offsets

The `members` action does `offset = params[:offset].to_i` without validating that it's non-negative. A negative offset (e.g., `?offset=-50`) will be passed to ActiveRecord's `.offset()`, which in PostgreSQL treats negative offsets as 0, but this behavior is database-dependent and could cause unexpected results. The offset should be clamped: `offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max`. Similarly, `limit` is not validated to be within a reasonable range (e.g., max 100 or 200), allowing a client to request `?limit=1000000` and potentially cause performance issues.

removeMember action in item view template won't bubble to controller correctly

The template `group_member.hbs` uses `{{action "removeMember" member}}` inside an `{{#each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` loop. The `itemView` is `Discourse.View` (from `group-member.js.es6`), not a controller. In Ember, actions in item views bubble to the view's controller, but since this is a plain View (not an ItemView with a specific controller), the action will bubble to the parent controller (the admin-group controller). However, the `removeMember` action expects `member` as a parameter, and in the `{{action}}` helper within an `{{#each}}` with `itemView`, the context may not correctly pass the `member` object. The action should be tested to ensure `member` is correctly passed; alternatively, use `{{action "removeMember" this}}` from within the view's context or use `targetObject` explicitly.

remove_member does not verify the user is actually a member before deleting

In `remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)` is called without checking whether the user is actually a member of the group. While `delete` on a non-member is a no-op at the database level, the action still returns `success_json` and calls `group.save`, which triggers unnecessary validations and callbacks. More importantly, if `user_id` refers to a non-existent user, the delete silently succeeds. The controller should verify the user exists and is a member, returning a 404 or 422 if not, so the admin UI can show an appropriate error.

update action always sets visible even when param is absent

The `update` action does `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally. If the client sends a PUT request without a `visible` parameter (e.g., only updating `alias_level`), `params[:visible]` is nil, and `nil == "true"` is false, so `visible` is set to false. This means any update that doesn't explicitly include `visible=true` will make the group invisible. The update should only modify `visible` if the parameter is present: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" if params.key?(:visible)`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
ensure_loaded! calls I18n.ensure_loaded! which is not thread-safe and races with translate_accelerator's load_locale

`FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` calls `I18n.ensure_loaded! l` for each locale in the fallback chain. However, `I18n.ensure_loaded!` (the class method added by translate_accelerator.rb line 62) is not synchronized with the `LOAD_MUTEX` that protects `load_locale`. The `ensure_loaded!` method does `@loaded_locales ||= []` and then `load_locale locale unless @loaded_locales.include?(locale)` without any mutex. Meanwhile, `load_locale` itself acquires `LOAD_MUTEX`, but the check `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` in `ensure_loaded!` happens outside the mutex. This creates a race condition: two threads can both call `ensure_loaded!` for the same locale, both see it's not in `@loaded_locales`, and both proceed to call `load_locale`. Inside `load_locale`, the mutex serializes them, but the second thread will still execute the full `load_translations` call because the `return if @loaded_locales.include?(locale)` check at the top of `load_locale` happens after acquiring the mutex but the first thread may not have finished appending to `@loaded_locales` yet (actually it does append inside the mutex, so this specific race is mitigated). However, the bigger issue is that `ensure_loaded!` is called from `ApplicationController#set_locale` on every request (line 159), and it calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` which is the accelerated version. But `I18n.ensure_loaded!` does not acquire `LOAD_MUTEX` for the `@loaded_locales.include?` check, so a thread can be in the middle of `load_locale` (holding the mutex, modifying `@loaded_locales`) while another thread reads `@loaded_locales` without the mutex in `ensure_loaded!`, leading to a potential `Concurrent::ModificationError` or inconsistent state. Additionally, `@loaded_locales ||= []` is not atomic; two threads can both initialize it, losing one thread's appends.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Comment 'order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb' is not a recognized Rails initializer directive and may not enforce load order

The first line of the initializer is `# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb`. Rails initializers in `config/initializers/` are loaded in alphabetical order by default. There is no built-in Rails mechanism that reads an `# order:` comment to control load order. If the intent is to ensure this initializer runs after `02-freedom_patches.rb` (which likely loads the translate_accelerator patch), the file should be named with a prefix that sorts after it (e.g., `03-i18n.rb` or similar), or the dependency should be handled explicitly. Since the file is named `i18n.rb`, it will load after `02-freedom_patches.rb` alphabetically (digits sort before letters in ASCII), so the order is accidentally correct, but the comment is misleading and suggests a non-existent feature. If someone renames the file or the freedom patches file, the load order could break silently, causing `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` to run before the translate_accelerator patch has reopened `I18n::Backend::Simple`, potentially leading to method resolution issues.

FallbackLocaleList#[] returns array but Hash subclass contract is violated, breaking I18n::Locale::Fallbacks compatibility

`FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides `[]` to return an array of locales (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`) instead of a single value. The i18n gem's `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` module expects `I18n.fallbacks` to respond to `[](locale)` returning either a single fallback locale or an array, but it also calls other Hash methods like `key?`, `[]=`, and iterates over the object in some code paths (e.g., `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks#compute` and `I18n.fallbacks.any?`). Because `FallbackLocaleList` is a Hash that never stores any keys (the `[]` method is overridden to compute dynamically), methods like `key?`, `keys`, `each`, and `empty?` will operate on the underlying empty hash and return incorrect results. For example, `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` calls `fallbacks = I18n.fallbacks[locale]` and then iterates, which works, but other code paths that check `I18n.fallbacks.key?(locale)` or `I18n.fallbacks[locale] ||= ...` will fail or behave unexpectedly. Additionally, `SiteSetting.default_locale` is called on every `[]` invocation, which hits the database/site settings cache on every translation fallback lookup, adding unnecessary overhead. The class should not inherit from Hash if it doesn't behave like one; it should be a plain object that implements the minimal interface expected by `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks`.

Fallbacks module included into wrong class, breaking I18n fallback resolution

The initializer does `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)`. At initializer load time, `I18n.backend` is an instance of `I18n::Backend::Simple`, so this includes Fallbacks into `I18n::Backend::Simple` itself. However, the translate_accelerator patch (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb) reopens `I18n::Backend::Simple` and overrides `available_locales`, and more importantly the fallback chain resolution in the i18n gem expects `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` to be mixed into the backend instance's class so that `translate` dispatches through the fallbacks module. Because `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` is set, the Fallbacks module's `translate` implementation calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`, but the module was included into the class before `I18n.fallbacks` was assigned and, critically, `I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Pluralization)` on line 5 already included Pluralization into Simple. The real problem: `I18n.backend.class` may not be `I18n::Backend::Simple` if another initializer or the Rails i18n railtie has already wrapped the backend (e.g., with `I18n::Backend::Chain` or a cache module), in which case Fallbacks gets included into the wrapper class but the fallback lookup still fails or the `translate` method resolution order puts the accelerator's `I18n.translate` override (which calls `translate_no_cache` directly, bypassing the backend's `translate` entirely) ahead of the fallback logic. Since `translate_accelerator.rb` aliases `I18n.translate` to `translate_no_cache` and calls it directly, the Fallbacks module's `translate` hook on the backend is never invoked for cached lookups, meaning fallbacks will silently not apply for any translation that goes through the accelerated path. The fallback chain will only work for translations that miss the accelerator cache and pass through `I18n::Backend::Base#translate`, which is inconsistent and will cause missing translations to render as 'translation missing' strings instead of falling back to the site default locale or English.

I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! called on every request, causing repeated fallback chain computation and DB lookups

`set_locale` is a `before_filter` that runs on every request. Line 159 calls `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, which invokes `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`. This method calls `self[I18n.locale]` which computes `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`. `SiteSetting.default_locale` is a site setting that may hit the database or a cache on every call. Then for each locale in the resulting array, it calls `I18n.ensure_loaded! l`, which checks `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` and potentially calls `load_locale`. While `load_locale` is idempotent (returns early if already loaded), the `ensure_loaded!` call still iterates over the fallback chain and performs the `SiteSetting.default_locale` lookup on every single request. This is unnecessary overhead: once a locale is loaded, it stays loaded for the process lifetime (until `reload!`). The `ensure_loaded!` call should be moved to a place where it runs once per locale change, or the `FallbackLocaleList` should cache the computed fallback chain per locale, or `set_locale` should only call `ensure_loaded!` when the locale actually changes.

Pluralization module included into I18n::Backend::Simple instead of I18n.backend, inconsistent with Fallbacks inclusion pattern

Line 5 does `I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Pluralization)` while line 9 does `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)`. These are inconsistent: one includes into the class directly, the other into the instance's class. If `I18n.backend` is not an instance of `I18n::Backend::Simple` (e.g., if Rails or another gem has wrapped it), the Pluralization module will be included into `Simple` but the Fallbacks module will be included into whatever class `I18n.backend` actually is. This means Pluralization might not be active on the actual backend instance. The correct approach is to include both modules into `I18n.backend.class` (or better, into `I18n::Backend::Base` so all backends get them), or use `I18n::Backend::Simple.include(...)` consistently for both. The previous `config/initializers/pluralization.rb` (removed in this PR) used `I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Pluralization)`, so the behavior for Pluralization is preserved, but the inconsistency with Fallbacks is a code smell that could cause subtle bugs if the backend class changes.

translate method checks @loaded_locales without mutex and without nil guard, causing NoMethodError on first call

The `translate` method (line 67-77) does `load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)`. If `@loaded_locales` has never been initialized (i.e., this is the first call to `translate` in the process and `ensure_loaded!` was not called first), `@loaded_locales` is nil, and calling `.include?` on nil raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'include?' for nil:NilClass`. The `ensure_loaded!` method added in this PR does `@loaded_locales ||= []` before the check, but `translate` does not. In the normal request flow, `ApplicationController#set_locale` calls `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` which calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` which initializes `@loaded_locales`, so by the time `translate` is called, `@loaded_locales` is set. However, there are many code paths where `I18n.translate` is called outside of a request cycle: background jobs, rake tasks, initializers, mailers, and model callbacks. Any of these that call `I18n.t` before the first web request will crash with NoMethodError. The `translate` method should also guard with `@loaded_locales ||= []` or use the same pattern as `ensure_loaded!`.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login.
